affectedPublicSurfaces: A new table `production_write_authorizations` `{id, shop_id, tiktok_product_id, mutation_kind, authorized_by, reason, created_at, expires_at, consumed_at, consumed_by_run_id}` plus an explicit revoked state — the first artifact in the system that can represent "the owner authorized this mutation, on this listing, once" (ADR-085 decision 6, the chain recorded at #1226). Single-use, expiring (default 24h from a documented setting, never null), scoped to exactly one shop, one product and one mutation kind.

The issuing path: an operator entry point that runs `services/tiktok/credential_binding.verify_capability_binding` FIRST and refuses to issue when the credential for that shop and capability is mis-bound (wrong `shop_cipher`, or a capability pointing at a different shop) — the #1290 "the product belongs to another seller" failure becomes impossible to AUTHORIZE, not merely impossible to execute. An authorization issued against a mis-provisioned credential is worse than none, because it looks like a green light.

The lookup the write path will use in #1336: given shop, product and mutation kind, return the matching unconsumed, unexpired, unrevoked row or nothing. Consumption is atomic — `consumed_at` and `consumed_by_run_id` set in the same transaction that claims the row, so two concurrent runs consume it exactly once and the loser observes the consumed state rather than a retryable error.
An operator revoke entry point that sets an explicit revoked state and preserves the row and its history — the audit is the point; revoke never deletes.

No seller-facing HTTP surface: no `/v1/*` route can create an authorization, asserted by test. Authorization is an operator action only. This slice builds the artifact and its lifecycle and does NOT wire it into the write path — that is #1336, so the resolver's four preconditions can be tested one at a time against a primitive that already works.

candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: Pre-merge: pytest with `PYTHONPATH` pinned to the worktree's `backend/src`; the concurrency and lookup cases run against real Postgres 16, never SQLite. Post-deploy: the sandbox shop and sandbox product only, via the operator entry point — no seller-facing route exists for issuing. The standing owner decision of 2026-08-21 forbids anything targeting Fujiwa Vietnam Store (`2b1da87b`), and this slice must not be the first thing to test that boundary. No production write is possible anywhere in the journey: the write path is not wired to this table until #1336, and the production-write capability remains default off.
candidateVerificationJourney.notes: Side effects stated plainly: the journey (a) inserts one row into `production_write_authorizations` for the sandbox shop, (b) marks it consumed via the lookup's atomic claim, and (c) touches nothing else — no TikTok call of any kind, no `workflow_runs`, no production credential resolved. The table is inert to the running release: no code path outside this wave references it until #1336 wires the resolver. apiSideEffectsInScope is FALSE in the sense the pairing rule protects — no public or production side effect — and the sandbox-scoped row inserts above are the complete list.
